data.completion_memo: Specified canonical per-record JSON format v1, UUID identities with preserved integer API aliases, multiline content, ordering/tombstones, complete data classification, content-based guards and external-change notifications, immutable receipts/evidence, checkout-local coordination and prepared-journal recovery. Documented independent-add/edit, overlapping-edit, delete-reference and equal-counter/different-content merge examples, plus migration/activation obligations and filesystem/concurrency limitations. Formal storage-text component and file binding updated through design read tokens. Reviewed against schema-14 inventory and full shared StorageBackend/ReadSnapshot interface. Task 17 may now implement this specification.

lines:
Execution order: step 06 of 13. Depends on Adashi task ID 15. Complete this prerequisite before starting.

Phase: Git-friendly text storage design.

Specify a project-local text representation; JSON is a candidate, not a preselected requirement:
- Prefer deterministic files organized by stable resource identity instead of a single frequently rewritten project document. Define field ordering, encoding/newlines, schema versions and canonical serialization; unchanged data must not be rewritten.
- Define collision-resistant IDs for resources created independently in different clones. Distinguish immutable identity from human task/QA numbers; specify compatibility and migration for current integer API IDs and cross-resource references.
- Specify representations for multiline Mermaid/DSL/SVG and other artifact content, explicit list ordering, deletions/tombstones where needed, and immutable QA/history evidence.
- Classify authoritative shared data, derived indexes/previews, local settings, secrets and transient state. Do not make users merge disposable caches, local absolute paths, or a global incrementing counter on every edit.
- Define content-based change/conflict detection across branches; equal numeric versions from different branches must not imply equal content. Handle operation receipts and expired advisory intents without false coordination across clones.
- Define structural and semantic validation after a Git merge, including delete-versus-reference conflicts and unresolved conflict markers. Define crash recovery and atomic multi-file publication.
- Update the formal storage design with the selected format, examples and limitations.

Acceptance: examples show independent additions and edits merging normally, while genuine overlapping edits and invalid references are detected without silent loss. Both clients can implement the same contract from this specification.

data.title: Storage 06/13 — Design a Git-mergeable text format and portable resource identities
